Position Title: Nursing: Tenure-Track Family Nurse Practitioner (Faculty) Job Category: Faculty Employment Type: Regular Job Profile: Assistant Professor Job Duties: POSITION : The Department of Nursing is recruiting for one probationary tenure-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant/Associate Professor with Family Nurse Practitioner (FNP) credentials and the disciplinary expertise needed to teach in undergraduate and graduate nursing programs. The appointment is for nine months (August through May), with the possibility of a summer appointment. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS : Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) degree from an accredited nursing program, Ph.D. in Nursing, or doctorate in a related field with a master’s degree in nursing from an accredited nursing program. Candidates near completion of the doctoral degree may be considered, contingent upon degree completion by the appointment start date. Unencumbered license as a registered nurse in the United States. Eligibility for immediate licensure as a registered nurse in Wisconsin. Current national certification as a Family Nurse Practitioner (FNP-BC or FNP-C). Eligibility to meet all clinical agency requirements, including health care provider CPR certification, required immunizations, and other agency-mandated verifications. Satisfactory background check clearance in accordance with applicable state statutes and clinical agency requirements. Clinical practice experience relevant to assigned teaching responsibilities. Demonstrated potential for teaching, scholarship, and service consistent with expectations for a tenure-track appointment. Demonstrated commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion, and belonging through teaching, clinical practice, scholarship, service, and/or community engagement. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS : Teaching experience in undergraduate and/or graduate nursing programs. Professional clinical experience as an Advanced Practice Registered Nurse (APRN). Experience teaching graduate nursing students in advanced practice nursing programs. Experience with clinical placement, preceptor collaboration, or graduate nursing clinical education. Evidence of scholarly activity, research, and/or professional dissemination. Demonstrated ability to integrate technology to enhance teaching and learning. Experience teaching in online, hybrid, simulation, and/or clinical learning environments. DUTIES : A typical faculty workload may include up to twenty-four (24) credits of undergraduate and graduate instruction per academic year delivered in face-to-face, hybrid, online, clinical, laboratory, and/or simulation settings. The University of Wisconsin–Eau Claire supports student-centered learning, interdisciplinary collaboration, leadership development, shared governance, professional growth, and innovative partnerships with community agencies and healthcare organizations. ABOUT US : College The College of Nursing advances the discipline through excellence in education, research, practice, and service. Guided by its core values of community, integrity, curiosity, and well-being, the college fosters a collaborative and student-centered environment that prepares nurses to lead, promote health, and improve health outcomes across populations and the lifespan. Faculty and staff are committed to creating meaningful learning experiences that support professional growth, innovation, scholarship, and compassionate care. The college values interdisciplinary collaboration, community engagement, rural health initiatives, global learning opportunities, and partnerships that strengthen healthcare outcomes throughout Wisconsin and beyond. Department The Department of Nursing offers four degree programs: the traditional Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN), the Bachelor of Science in Nursing Completion (BSNC), the Master of Science in Nursing (MSN), and the Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP). All programs are accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education. Faculty engage in high-impact teaching, scholarship, clinical practice, and service that support student success and advance the profession of nursing. Opportunities exist for faculty and students to collaborate in faculty-mentored scholarly projects, simulation and clinical learning experiences, intercultural immersion opportunities, community-engaged partnerships, and innovative healthcare initiatives.

The department also has an active speech, language, and hearing clinic including 16 treatment rooms with remote observation capabilities, as well as numerous community collaborations for service delivery.
